questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical containers kept at the same temperature carry the same gas with different molecular mean free paths $l_1$ and $l_2$. The gas from the first container is completely transferred into the second at the same temperature. What is the molecular mean free path of the resultant mixture in the second container?

questions.q: What is the average kinetic energy of molecules of an ideal gas leaking freely through an orifice of a container which has $N$ molecules at pressure $P$ in volume $V$ ?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical boxes contain the same ideal gas. Let $\left(n_1, \lambda_1, T_1\right)$ and $\left(n_2\right.$, $\lambda_2, T_2$ ) be the number density, mean free path and temperature of the gas in the first and the second box, respectively. One of the boxes is emptied into the other one. What will be the mean free path $\lambda$ and temperature $T$ of the gas now?

Average kinetic energy of $\mathrm{O}_2$ molecules < Average kinetic energy of $\mathrm{N}_2$ molecules
Average kinetic energy of $\mathrm{O}_2$ molecules > Average kinetic energy of $\mathrm{N}_2$ molecules

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A jar is filled with two monoatomic non-interacting gases $A$ and $B$ with total masses $M_A$ and $M_B$, respectively. The molar mass of $A$ is double the molar mass of $B$. If the jar is kept at temperature $T$, what is the ratio of the total pressure of the combined gas to the partial pressure due to the gas $A$?
questions.solution:
Let $m_A$ and $m_B$ be the molar masses of gases $A$ and $B$ respectively.

Given $m_A = 2m_B$.

Number of moles of gas $A$, $n_A = \dfrac{M_A}{m_A}$

Number of moles of gas $B$, $n_B = \dfrac{M_B}{m_B}$

According to Dalton's law of partial pressures, the partial pressure of a gas is proportional to its number of moles.

Partial pressure of $A$, $P_A = \dfrac{n_A RT}{V}$

Total pressure, $P = \dfrac{(n_A + n_B) RT}{V}$

The ratio of the total pressure to the partial pressure of $A$ is:

$\dfrac{P}{P_A} = \dfrac{n_A + n_B}{n_A} = 1 + \dfrac{n_B}{n_A}$

Substituting the values of $n_A$ and $n_B$:

$\dfrac{P}{P_A} = 1 + \dfrac{\dfrac{M_B}{m_B}}{\dfrac{M_A}{m_A}} = 1 + \dfrac{M_B}{M_A} \times \dfrac{m_A}{m_B}$

Since $m_A = 2m_B$, we get $\dfrac{m_A}{m_B} = 2$.

$\dfrac{P}{P_A} = 1 + 2\dfrac{M_B}{M_A}$

Answer: $1 + 2\dfrac{M_B}{M_A}$
